Tomato Late Blight.description: Aggressive oomycete disease that spreads fast in cool, wet weather and can destroy a plant within days.
symptoms: White fuzzy mold on leaf undersides in humid mornings
Firm brown greasy lesions on fruit
Rapid blackening and collapse of stems
causes: Spread by wind-blown spores and splashing water
treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately — do not compost
Apply a copper-based fungicide or chlorothalonil at first sign
Avoid overhead watering
Improve airflow by staking/pruning
prevention: Rotate away from tomato/potato for 2-3 years
care_tips: Water at soil level in the morning

Tomato Early Blight.description: Common fungal disease causing target-ring spots, usually starting on older lower leaves.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (bullseye pattern) on older leaves
Leaf drop starting from the bottom
causes: Spread by wind and rain splash
Survives in soil and old plant debris
treatment: Remove infected lower leaves promptly
Apply chlorothalonil, copper, or mancozeb fungicide at first symptoms
Mulch to stop soil splashing onto leaves

Healthy Leaf.description: No disease detected — normal healthy tomato leaf growth.
treatment: No treatment needed
prevention: Continue current watering, sunlight, and nutrition routine

Potato Early Blight.description: Fungal disease causing target-pattern leaf spots; caused by the same fungus as tomato early blight.
symptoms: Brown target-pattern spots on older leaves
Occasional dark sunken lesions on tubers
causes: More severe on stressed or nutrient-deficient plants
treatment: Remove infected foliage
Apply chlorothalonil, copper, or mancozeb fungicide
Maintain balanced nitrogen — avoid both excess and deficiency
prevention: Balanced fertilization to avoid plant stress

Potato Late Blight.description: The disease behind the Irish potato famine — extremely aggressive, can wipe out a field within days in cool wet weather.
symptoms: Water-soaked dark green/brown leaf lesions with white fuzzy mold underneath
Rapid blackening and collapse of foliage
causes: Spread by spores in cool wet weather
treatment: Destroy infected plants immediately
Apply preventive copper-based or chlorothalonil fungicide before outbreaks in high-risk weather
Harvest early if an outbreak is detected
Avoid harvesting in wet conditions
prevention: Hill soil to fully cover tubers
Destroy cull piles and volunteer plants
care_tips: Watch weather forecasts for cool/wet blight-favorable conditions
Scout fields regularly during risk periods

Healthy Leaf.description: No disease detected — normal healthy potato leaf growth.
treatment: No treatment needed
prevention: Continue current watering and nutrition routine
care_tips: Hill soil around stems as they grow

Apple Scab.description: The most common fungal disease of apple trees, reducing fruit quality and causing early leaf drop.
symptoms: Olive-green velvety spots on leaves turning black and scabby
Dark scabby lesions on fruit surface
causes: Spread by wind and rain in spring
treatment: Apply fungicide (captan, myclobutanil, or sulfur-based) starting at bud break
Rake and destroy fallen leaves each autumn
prevention: Preventive fungicide sprays during wet spring weather

Apple Black Rot.description: Fungal disease causing 'frogeye' leaf spot, fruit rot, and branch cankers.
symptoms: Brown/purple circular leaf spots with concentric rings (frogeye pattern)
Fruit rot starting at the blossom end, turning black and mummified
causes: Enters through wounds or dead wood
treatment: Prune out and destroy cankered branches and mummified fruit
Apply fungicide during the growing season
prevention: Maintain tree vigor with proper fertilization/watering
Remove mummified fruit from tree and ground
care_tips: Inspect for cankers each dormant season

Healthy Leaf.description: No disease detected — normal healthy apple leaf growth.
treatment: No treatment needed

Corn Common Rust.description: Fungal disease producing reddish-brown pustules on leaves; usually minor unless infection is severe or early.
symptoms: Small reddish-brown to cinnamon raised pustules on both leaf surfaces
Severe cases cause yellowing and leaf death
treatment: Apply a strobilurin or triazole fungicide if infection is severe or early
Minor infections usually don't need treatment
prevention: Avoid very early planting in high-risk cool/humid regions
care_tips: Scout fields weekly during cool humid periods

Healthy Leaf.description: No disease detected — normal healthy corn leaf growth.
treatment: No treatment needed

Grape Black Rot.description: Serious fungal disease that can destroy an entire grape crop if left untreated.
symptoms: Small tan/brown circular leaf spots with dark borders
causes: Overwinters in mummified berries and infected wood
Spread by rain splash in warm wet weather
treatment: Remove and destroy mummified berries and infected canes during dormant pruning
Apply fungicide (mancozeb or myclobutanil) from bud break through fruit set
prevention: Remove all mummified fruit from vine and ground
Preventive fungicide program during wet spring weather
care_tips: Clean vineyard floor each dormant season
Monitor closely from bloom through fruit set

Healthy Leaf.description: No disease detected — normal healthy grape leaf growth.
treatment: No treatment needed

Pepper Bacterial Spot.description: Bacterial disease causing leaf and fruit spotting; can cause significant defoliation in warm wet conditions.
symptoms: Small water-soaked leaf spots turning brown/black with a yellow halo
Spots merging and causing leaf drop
Raised scabby brown spots on fruit
causes: Spread by splashing water, wind-driven rain, and contaminated seed/tools
Favored by warm wet humid weather
treatment: Apply copper-based bactericide (often combined with mancozeb, since copper resistance is common)
Remove and destroy infected plant debris
Avoid working in fields when wet

Healthy Leaf.description: No disease detected — normal healthy pepper leaf growth.
treatment: No treatment needed
care_tips: Water at soil level, avoid wetting foliage

Citrus Canker.description: Highly contagious bacterial disease; a regulated quarantine pathogen in many regions.
symptoms: Raised corky brown lesions with a yellow halo on leaves, fruit, and twigs
Premature leaf and fruit drop in severe cases
causes: Spread by wind-driven rain, contaminated tools, and citrus leafminer wounds
treatment: Prune and destroy infected plant material
Apply copper-based bactericide, especially after wind/rain events
Control citrus leafminer
This is a regulated disease in many regions — contact your local agricultural extension office, as reporting/removal may be legally required
care_tips: Report suspected outbreaks to local authorities if in a canker-free region

Citrus Greening (HLB).description: One of the most destructive citrus diseases worldwide, spread by the Asian citrus psyllid; currently has no cure.
symptoms: Blotchy, asymmetric yellow mottling across the leaf midrib (unlike nutrient deficiency)
Small, lopsided, bitter fruit that stays green at the bottom
causes: Transmitted exclusively by the Asian citrus psyllid
treatment: No cure currently exists
Management focuses on removing and destroying infected trees to reduce spread, and controlling the psyllid vector
Contact your local agricultural extension immediately — this is a regulated quarantine disease in most citrus regions
care_tips: Inspect new flush growth for psyllids and mottled yellowing
Avoid moving citrus plant material between regions

Citrus Black Spot.description: Fungal disease that mainly affects fruit appearance and marketability; regulated in many export markets.
symptoms: Small dark brown/black spots with grey centers on fruit rind
causes: Favored by warm wet summer conditions
treatment: Apply copper-based or strobilurin fungicide during fruit development
Remove fallen leaves/debris that harbor the fungus
prevention: Good grove sanitation — remove fallen leaves and fruit
Preventive fungicide sprays during wet season
care_tips: Monitor fruit closely from early development through harvest

Healthy Leaf.description: No disease detected — normal healthy citrus leaf growth.
treatment: No treatment needed
prevention: Continue current care routine, monitor for psyllids

Rice Blast.description: One of the most destructive rice diseases worldwide, capable of causing total crop loss under favorable conditions.
symptoms: Diamond/spindle-shaped lesions with grey centers and brown borders on leaves
'Neck blast' — grain heads break and turn white/empty
causes: Favored by high humidity, excess nitrogen, and dense planting
treatment: Apply fungicide (tricyclazole, azoxystrobin, or propiconazole) at first sign of lesions
Avoid excess nitrogen application
Drain excess standing water if humidity is very high
prevention: Avoid excessive nitrogen — use split doses
Remove infected crop residue after harvest
care_tips: Scout fields regularly during humid periods

Healthy Leaf.description: No disease detected — normal healthy rice leaf growth.
treatment: No treatment needed
